questions.question: Which of the following pins on the 8051 microcontroller is used for transmitting serial data (TXD)?
questions.explanation:
The pin labeled TXD corresponds to P3.1 in the pin‑function table. (Source Page: [15])  

---

questions.question: How many bytes of on‑chip RAM are available in a standard 8051 microcontroller?
questions.explanation:
The summary states that the 8051 has 128 bytes of on‑chip data memory. (Source Page: [12])  

---

questions.question: What is the size of the address bus in the 8051 microcontroller?
questions.explanation:
The 8051 features a 16‑bit address bus, allowing access to 64 KB of memory. (Source Page: [12])  

---

questions.question: In the given delay routine, how many times is the DJNZ instruction executed?
questions.explanation:
The register R3 is loaded with #200, so DJNZ loops 200 iterations. (Source Page: [45])

questions.question: What is the total calculated delay of the program shown, assuming a crystal frequency of 11.0592 MHz?
questions.explanation:
Adding the three timing components gives a total delay of 437.658 µs. (Source Page: [45])

questions.question: Which pin function listed below is associated with the external interrupt INT0?
questions.explanation:
The table shows “(-INT0)” next to P3.2, indicating INT0 is on that pin. (Source Page: [15])

questions.question: The 8051’s data bus width determines how many bits can be transferred in one operation. What is that width?
questions.explanation:
The summary explicitly mentions an 8‑bit data bus. (Source Page: [12])  

---

questions.question: Which of the following pins is designated for the external memory read (RD) signal?
questions.explanation:
The pin table lists “(-RD)” next to P3.7, indicating the RD signal. (Source Page: [15])

questions.question: If the 8051’s on‑chip RAM is exhausted, which type of memory can be accessed next for data storage?

options.D: No additional memory can be accessed

questions.explanation:
With a 16‑bit address bus the 8051 can address up to 64 KB of external RAM and ROM. (Source Page: [12])

questions.question: In the delay sub‑routine, what is the purpose of the RET instruction?

options.B: To return control to the calling routine

questions.explanation: RET ends the sub‑routine and returns to the instruction after the ACALL. (Source Page: [45])
